title: Spinal Motion Restriction, Head-Injury Targets and Complications

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already log roll, size collars and secure patients. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Weigh the risks of motion restriction against the benefit
  2. Handle hard cases: seated patients, rapid extrication, helmets
  3. Apply BC's TBI targets and recognize autonomic dysreflexia

Textbook: Chapter 25, PDF pages 2133–2162
slides.say: Welcome back. Last lesson was about assessment; today is about packaging, and what you think about while you do it. You already know how to log roll, size a collar and secure a patient, so we won't repeat every step. As a PCP, you'll weigh the risks of motion restriction against its benefits, handle harder cases like seated patients, rapid extrication, helmets and pregnancy, and apply BC's targets when the spinal patient also has a head injury. We'll finish with autonomic dysreflexia, and with back pain that isn't from trauma.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。上节课讲评估，今天讲固定包装，以及做的时候要想什么。你们已经会轴线翻身、选颈托尺寸、固定病人，所以不再逐步重复。作为 PCP，你要权衡脊柱活动限制的利弊，处理更难的情况，比如坐位病人、快速解救、头盔和孕妇，并在脊柱病人同时有颅脑外伤时运用 BC 的目标值。最后讲自主神经反射异常，以及非创伤性腰背痛。

slides.title: Motion restriction is not harmless
slides.body:
Spinal motion restriction, not "immobilization"

  • A backboard is a moving tool; it doesn't protect the spine
  • Costs: pain, anxiety, restricted breathing, aspiration
  • Rigid collar: may raise intracranial pressure
  • Skin breakdown: 32% of cord injuries within 24 hours
  • Goal: no more than the platinum 10 minutes on scene
slides.say: First, a change in language: spinal motion restriction, not immobilization. You can't truly immobilize a spine outside hospital, and a backboard is mainly a tool for moving people; it doesn't protect the spine by itself. Motion restriction also has costs. It hurts the back of the head and the lower back, makes people anxious, limits breathing, and raises the risk of aspiration. A rigid collar may raise the pressure inside the skull. And thirty-two percent of patients with a cord injury develop a skin lesion within twenty-four hours. So use it when indicated, keep it short, and aim for the platinum ten minutes on scene.
slides.sayZh: 先改个说法：叫“脊柱活动限制”，不叫“脊柱固定”。在院外根本无法真正固定脊柱；长板主要是搬运工具，本身并不保护脊柱。活动限制也有代价：枕部和腰骶部会痛，病人会焦虑，呼吸受限，误吸风险增加。硬颈托可能升高颅内压。而百分之三十二的脊髓损伤病人在二十四小时内出现皮肤损伤。所以有指征才用、时间尽量短，现场时间以“白金十分钟”为目标。

slides.title: BC's steps, and the order that matters
slides.body:
Hands on the head→Hard collar→Device + foam blocks→Secure the body
  • The collar adds to your hands; it never replaces them
  • Book: strap the torso first, then pelvis and legs, head last
  • Adults: 1–5 cm of padding under the back of the head
  • Children: pad under the torso (big head bends the neck)
  • BC: do not tape the head
slides.say: Here's BC's Spinal Management sequence, the same at every licence level: manual stabilization, a hard collar, a spinal device with foam blocks, and securing the body. Two details matter. One, the collar only adds to your hands; keep holding until the head is blocked. Two, the book secures the torso first, then the pelvis and legs, and the head last; if the head is fixed and the heavy body slides, the neck takes the strain. Pad the gaps: an adult often needs one to five centimetres under the back of the head, and a child, with a big head, needs padding under the torso. And in BC, don't tape the head.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 脊柱管理的步骤，所有执照级别都一样：徒手稳定、硬颈托、脊柱固定装置加泡沫头块、固定身体。有两个细节很重要。第一，颈托只是辅助你的双手，头部用头块固定好之前不要松手。第二，书里先固定躯干，再固定骨盆和腿，最后才固定头部；如果头先固定、沉重的身体再一滑，颈部就要承受拉力。要把空隙垫好：成人枕部下面常需垫一到五厘米；小孩头大，垫子要放在躯干下面。在 BC，不要用胶带固定头部。

slides.title: Neutral alignment: know when to stop
slides.body:
Neutral gives the cord the most room

Stop and hold the head where you found it if moving it causes:

  • Neck muscle spasm
  • Resistance to movement
  • More pain
  • Numbness, tingling or weakness
slides.say: Neutral alignment, with the eyes looking straight ahead and the head in line with the body, gives the spinal cord the most room, so we aim for it. But never force it. As you gently move the head, stop if the neck muscles are in spasm, if you feel resistance, if the pain increases, or if new numbness, tingling or weakness appears. Then support and secure the head where you found it. Think of a cracked, bent garden hose: straightening it gently helps, but forcing it could split it. Document why you didn't reach neutral, and recheck the limbs after every move.
slides.sayZh: 中立位，即双眼平视前方、头与身体成一直线，能给脊髓最大的空间，所以我们以它为目标。但绝不要强求。轻轻移动头部时，如果颈部肌肉痉挛、感到阻力、疼痛加重，或出现新的麻木、刺痛或无力，就停下，在发现时的位置支撑并固定头部。想象一根有裂缝又弯着的水管：轻轻拉直有帮助，硬掰可能让它裂开。记录没能摆到中立位的原因，每次移动后都复查四肢。

slides.q: You gently turn a patient's head toward neutral. She says her neck pain is much worse, and her fingers start tingling. What do you do?
options: Keep going: the collar only fits in neutral
Stop and support the head where it is now
Apply gentle traction to open up the spine
Ask her to move her head to neutral herself
slides.say: Quick check. You gently turn a patient's head toward neutral. She says her neck pain is much worse, and her fingers start tingling. What do you do? A, keep going, because the collar only fits in neutral. B, stop and support the head where it is now. C, apply gentle traction to open up the spine. D, ask her to move her head to neutral herself. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 快速检查。你把病人的头轻轻转向中立位，她说颈痛明显加重，手指开始刺痛。你怎么做？A 继续，因为颈托只能在中立位戴；B 停下，在现在的位置支撑头部；C 轻轻牵引，把脊柱拉开；D 让她自己把头转到中立位。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. More pain and new tingling tell you to stop and support the head where it is; forcing it could injure the cord. A is wrong: neutral is a goal, not worth an injury, and towel rolls and padding can hold the head in place. C is wrong because traction can pull apart an unstable injury. D is wrong because a patient with new neuro symptoms shouldn't move her own neck.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。疼痛加重和新出现的刺痛，就是让你停下、在原位支撑头部的信号；硬掰可能损伤脊髓。A 错：中立位是目标，不值得为它造成损伤，可以用毛巾卷和垫子把头固定在原位。C 错，牵引可能把不稳定的损伤拉开。D 错，出现新神经症状的病人不应该自己活动颈部。

slides.title: Getting them onto the device
slides.body:
Least to most spine movement:

Scoop→6-person lift→Straddle lift→Log roll
  • Scoop: good on ice; you can't see the back
  • Log roll: roll away from the injured side, check the back
  • Late pregnancy: tilt the board 15–20° to the left
  • Toddler in an undamaged car seat: can often stay in it
slides.say: How do you get the patient onto the device? The book ranks the methods from least to most spine movement: the scoop stretcher, the six-person lift, the straddle lift, and the four-person log roll, though nobody knows if the differences really matter. The scoop works well on hard, slippery ground like ice, but you can't see the back. If you log roll, roll away from the injured side and check the back. In the third trimester, tilt the whole board fifteen to twenty degrees to the left, so the uterus doesn't press on the big vein and drop the pressure. A toddler can often stay in an undamaged car seat.
slides.sayZh: 怎么把病人弄上装置？书里按脊柱移动从少到多排序：铲式担架、六人抬移、跨立抬移、四人轴线翻身，不过没人知道这些差别有没有临床意义。铲式担架在冰面这类坚硬湿滑的地面上很好用，但看不到背部。如果轴线翻身，要翻向远离伤侧并检查背部。孕晚期要把整块板向左倾斜十五到二十度，避免子宫压迫大静脉导致血压下降。幼儿如果儿童座椅完好，通常可以留在座椅里。

slides.title: Seated patients and rapid extrication
slides.body:
Low riska decision rule may clear theme.g. Canadian C-Spine
Stable, needs restrictioncollar + vest-type devicethen the long board
Urgentrapid extrication, about 2 minmore spine movement
  • Rapid only if: unsafe, can't assess, urgent care or transport
  • Or the patient blocks access to a worse patient
slides.say: Patients sitting in a car need a decision. With a low-risk mechanism, a rule like the Canadian C-Spine rule may show they don't need motion restriction at all. If they're stable but do need it, use a collar and a vest-type extrication device to move them onto the long board. Rapid extrication takes about two minutes, but it moves the spine more, so save it for real urgency: an unsafe scene, a patient you can't assess in the car, care that needs them lying flat, a need for immediate transport, or a patient blocking you from someone worse. As a PCP, that's a judgment call you must be able to defend.
slides.sayZh: 坐在车里的病人需要你做决定。受伤机制低危时，加拿大颈椎规则这类工具可能显示根本不需要限制。如果病人稳定但确实需要，就用颈托加背心式解救装置把他移到长板上。快速解救大约两分钟，但脊柱移动更多，所以只留给真正紧急的情况：现场不安全、在车里无法评估、需要平卧才能做的处理、需要立即转运，或病人挡住了伤得更重的人。作为 PCP，这是一个你必须能说清理由的判断。

slides.title: Helmets: leave on or take off?
slides.body:
Remove it if…Leave it on if…
It doesn't hold the head snuglyThe head fits snugly inside
You can't manage the airway, even with the face mask offThe airway is reachable
It stops proper motion restrictionIt can be secured to the device

Football and hockey: helmet and shoulder pads come off together or not at all. Always two rescuers.
slides.say: A well-fitted helmet actually helps hold the head still, and taking it off always moves the neck a little. So take it off only if it doesn't hold the head snugly, if you still can't manage the airway after removing the face mask, or if it stops you from restricting motion for transport. Leave it on if the head fits snugly, the airway is reachable, and the helmet can be secured to the device. In football and ice hockey, the helmet and shoulder pads come off together or not at all; removing only one throws the neck out of line. Removal always takes two trained rescuers.
slides.sayZh: 合适的头盔其实有助于稳住头部，而摘头盔总会让颈部有些移动。所以只有在头盔固定不住头部、拆掉面罩后仍无法处理气道、或妨碍转运时的活动限制时才摘。如果头在盔内贴合、气道可及、头盔能固定到装置上，就保留。橄榄球和冰球的头盔与护肩要么一起摘、要么都不摘，只摘一样会让颈部偏离轴线。摘头盔永远需要两名受过训练的施救者。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: spine plus head injury
slides.body:
BC TBI protocol: head trauma + altered LOC. GCS 13+ mild, 9–12 moderate, 8 or less severe.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Oxygen: SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Assist ventilations if needed
  • Head of the bed up 30 degrees
  • Loosen the hard collar

PCP adds

  • Blood sugar 4.0–8.0 mmol/L
  • Systolic BP above 120 mmHg
  • IV TKVO if systolic is above 120
  • TXA: contraindicated in isolated TBI
slides.say: Many spinal patients also have a head injury, and BC's Traumatic Brain Injury protocol changes your packaging. Suspect a brain injury with head trauma and an altered level of consciousness; a GCS of eight or less is severe. Every licence level gives oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher, assists breathing if needed, raises the head of the bed to thirty degrees, and loosens the hard collar. The PCP adds: keep the blood sugar between four and eight, keep the systolic above one hundred twenty, and run the IV to keep the vein open, or TKVO, once the systolic is above one hundred twenty. TXA is contraindicated for an isolated head injury.
slides.sayZh: 很多脊柱伤病人同时有颅脑外伤，而 BC 的颅脑外伤（TBI）流程会改变你的固定方式。有头部外伤且意识水平改变，就要怀疑脑损伤；GCS 八分及以下为重度。所有执照级别都要给氧使血氧维持在九十四以上，需要时辅助通气，床头抬高三十度，并松开硬颈托。PCP 另外要：血糖维持在四到八之间，收缩压维持在一百二十以上；收缩压高于一百二十后，静脉以 TKVO（保持静脉通畅）速度维持。单纯颅脑外伤禁用 TXA。

slides.q: A motorcyclist with a suspected neck injury has GCS 10 and BP 108/70. You're the PCP. Which plan matches BC's TBI protocol?
options: Keep the collar tight and the stretcher flat
Head of bed up 30°, loosen the collar, aim for systolic above 120
Give TXA for the head injury
IV at TKVO, because 108 is a normal pressure
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. A motorcyclist with a suspected neck injury has a GCS of ten and a blood pressure of one hundred eight over seventy. You're the PCP. Which plan matches BC's TBI protocol? A, keep the collar tight and the stretcher flat. B, raise the head of the bed to thirty degrees, loosen the collar, and aim for a systolic above one hundred twenty. C, give TXA for the head injury. D, run the IV at TKVO, because one hundred eight is a normal pressure. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名疑似颈部受伤的摩托车手，GCS 十分，血压一百零八比七十。你是 PCP，哪个方案符合 BC 的 TBI 流程？A 颈托保持紧、担架放平；B 床头抬高三十度、松开颈托，目标收缩压一百二十以上；C 为颅脑外伤给 TXA；D 静脉 TKVO 维持，因为一百零八是正常血压。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. BC's TBI protocol raises the head of the bed to thirty degrees and loosens the collar at every licence level, and the PCP aims for a systolic above one hundred twenty. A might suit a spinal injury alone, but not with a head injury in BC. C is wrong because TXA is for shock from blood loss, which he doesn't have, and it's contraindicated in an isolated head injury. D is wrong because one hundred eight is below the TBI target; TKVO is for patients already above one hundred twenty.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 的 TBI 流程要求所有执照级别把床头抬高三十度、松开颈托；PCP 还要把收缩压维持在一百二十以上。A 也许适用于单纯脊柱损伤，但在 BC 合并颅脑外伤时不行。C 错，TXA 用于失血性休克，他没有，而且单纯颅脑外伤禁用 TXA。D 错，一百零八低于 TBI 的目标值；TKVO 是给收缩压已高于一百二十的病人的。

slides.title: Autonomic dysreflexia
slides.body:
Old cord injury above T4–T6 + a trigger below = BP crisis

  • Systolic over 200, diastolic 130 or more
  • Headache; flushed, sweaty skin above the injury
  • Pale, cool skin below; slow pulse; stuffy nose
  • Triggers: full bladder, catheter problem, tight clothing, sharp object
  • Your job: find and remove the trigger
slides.say: Now a complication of an old spinal cord injury. Autonomic dysreflexia happens mostly with injuries above T4 to T6. Something irritates the body below the injury: a full bladder, a catheter problem, tight clothing, a sharp object, or a pressure sore. The signal can't reach the brain, so the sympathetic system fires without control. Below the injury, vessels clamp down and the skin is pale and cool. The systolic can climb over two hundred, with a diastolic of one hundred thirty or more. The brain tries to slow the heart, so the pulse is slow, and the skin above the injury is flushed and sweaty. Your job: find and remove the trigger.
slides.sayZh: 再讲一个陈旧性脊髓损伤的并发症：自主神经反射异常，多见于 T4 到 T6 以上的损伤。损伤以下有东西在刺激身体：膀胱胀满、导尿管出问题、衣服太紧、尖锐物或压疮。信号传不到大脑，交感神经就失控地放电。损伤以下血管收紧，皮肤苍白发凉；收缩压可超过两百，舒张压一百三十或更高。大脑想让心跳慢下来，所以脉搏慢，损伤以上皮肤潮红出汗。你的任务：找到并去除诱因。

slides.title: Back pain without trauma
slides.body:
• 60–90% of people get low back pain at some point
  • Most stressed spot: L4–L5; most cases have no clear cause
  • Disc herniation: often men 30–50, poor lifting; L4–L5, L5–S1
  • Look for nerve signs: weakness, numbness, tingling
  • Thin bones: fracture with minor force; cancer: pathologic fracture
  • Severe spasm: a scoop stretcher may be kindest
slides.say: Not every back call is trauma. Sixty to ninety percent of people get low back pain at some point, and the most stressed spot is L4 to L5. Most cases have no clear cause, though muscle and ligament strains are common. A herniated disc is more common in men aged thirty to fifty after poor lifting, usually at L4 to L5 or L5 to S1. As a PCP, look for the dangerous ones: new weakness, numbness or tingling. Older patients with thin bones can fracture a vertebra with little force, and cancer in the spine can cause a fracture that presses on the cord. For severe spasm, a scoop stretcher may be kindest.
slides.sayZh: 不是每个腰背痛都是创伤。百分之六十到九十的人一生中会有腰痛，受力最大的位置是 L4 到 L5。多数查不出确切原因，肌肉和韧带拉伤很常见。椎间盘突出多见于三十到五十岁、搬抬姿势不当的男性，常见于 L4–L5 或 L5–S1。作为 PCP，要找出危险的情况：新出现的无力、麻木或刺痛。骨质疏松的老人很小的外力就可能压缩椎骨；脊柱里的癌症也可能造成骨折并压迫脊髓。肌肉痉挛严重时，用铲式担架搬运可能最温和。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Decide with NEXUS or Canadian C-Spine; same at every level
  • Multi-trauma → full SMR; NEXUS positive or high-risk → simple SMR
  • Book shows taping the head; BC: do not tape the head
  • Book avoids raising the head; BC TBI: head of bed 30°, loosen collar
  • Atropine, benzodiazepines, dopamine, norepinephrine: not on the BC exam drug list

Simple SMR: collar on, head not taped, patient on the stretcher mattress (not a scoop).
slides.say: Here's where the book and BC differ. In BC, every licence level decides on motion restriction with NEXUS or the Canadian C-Spine rule. BC's adult decision matrix gives full motion restriction to multi-trauma patients. A positive NEXUS, or a high-risk patient, such as someone over sixty-five, gets simple motion restriction: a collar, the head not taped, and the patient on the stretcher mattress, not a scoop stretcher. The book shows tape across the head; BC says don't tape the head. The book avoids raising the head of the stretcher, but with a head injury, BC's TBI protocol raises it to thirty degrees and loosens the collar. And the book's atropine, benzodiazepines, dopamine and norepinephrine aren't on the BC licensing exam.
slides.sayZh: 这里是书和 BC 不一样的地方。在 BC，所有执照级别都用 NEXUS 或加拿大颈椎规则决定是否限制脊柱活动。BC 的成人决策表规定：多发伤病人做完全脊柱活动限制；NEXUS 阳性、或高危病人（比如六十五岁以上），做简易脊柱活动限制：戴颈托、头部不用胶带固定、病人躺在担架床垫上，不用铲式担架。书里会用胶带固定头部；BC 规定不要用胶带固定头部。书里避免抬高担架床头，但合并颅脑外伤时，BC 的 TBI 流程要求抬高到三十度并松开颈托。书里的阿托品、苯二氮卓类、多巴胺和去甲肾上腺素执照考试都不考。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Strapped flat: harder breathing, aspiration risk; reassess
  • Spine + head injury: follow the TBI targets, not habit
  • Rapid extrication only for real urgency: document why
  • Pressure sores start within hours: keep board time short
  • Pulse, motor, sensation in all four limbs after every move
  • Shock care: IV en route, don't hold the scene
slides.say: So what's new for you as a PCP? First, a patient strapped flat breathes less well and can't protect the airway if they vomit, so reassess breathing after packaging and keep suction ready. Second, with a head injury, follow the TBI targets, not old habits. Third, rapid extrication is a decision you'll need to defend, so use it only for real urgency and document why. Fourth, keep board time short, because pressure sores start within hours. Fifth, check pulse, movement and feeling in all four limbs after every move. And for shock, start your IV en route rather than holding the scene.
slides.sayZh: 那么作为 PCP，有哪些新的注意事项？第一，平绑在板上的病人呼吸会变差，呕吐时也无法自己保护气道，所以固定后要复评呼吸、备好吸引器。第二，合并颅脑外伤时，按 TBI 目标值处理，而不是按老习惯。第三，快速解救是要能说清理由的决定，只在真正紧急时用，并记录原因。第四，压疮几小时内就开始，在板上的时间要短。第五，每次移动后都检查四肢的脉搏、运动和感觉。处理休克时，在途中开静脉，不要拖在现场。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Motion restriction has costs: use it when indicated, keep it short, reassess
  2. Torso before head; never force neutral; don't tape the head (BC)
  3. Spine + head injury: 30°, loosen collar, systolic > 120, sugar 4.0–8.0

Next: Chapter 26, Thoracic Injuries
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: motion restriction has costs, including harder breathing, aspiration and pressure sores, so use it when NEXUS or the Canadian C-Spine rule says to, keep it short, and reassess. Two: secure the torso before the head, never force neutral against pain or new symptoms, and in BC, don't tape the head. Three: when the spinal patient also has a head injury, raise the head of the bed to thirty degrees and loosen the collar, and as a PCP, keep the systolic above one hundred twenty and the sugar between four and eight. Next chapter: thoracic injuries. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，活动限制有代价，包括呼吸变差、误吸和压疮，所以按 NEXUS 或加拿大颈椎规则有指征才用，时间尽量短，并反复复评。二，先固定躯干再固定头部；疼痛或新症状出现时绝不硬摆中立位；在 BC 不要用胶带固定头部。三，脊柱病人合并颅脑外伤时，床头抬高三十度、松开颈托；作为 PCP，还要维持收缩压一百二十以上、血糖四到八。下一章讲胸部创伤。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
